title: Lumipulse plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio reduced indeterminate results in a specialty cohort
bottomLine: In 208 symptomatic specialty-care patients, the automated p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio had an AUC of 0.932 against CSF or amyloid PET and produced fewer indeterminate results than p-tau217 alone, but its cutoffs were derived in the same cohort.
regulatoryStatus: Research evaluation; assay-specific clinical claims require applicable authorization
brief30: The study supports a two-cutoff, three-zone interpretation for an automated plasma ratio in symptomatic specialty care. The ratio retained high agreement with CSF or amyloid PET and reduced the gray zone relative to p-tau217 alone. It does not establish performance in primary care or validate a universally transferable threshold.
studyDesign: Single-center symptomatic cohort; 208 adults aged 51–88 years, including 7 with subjective cognitive decline, 150 with MCI, 12 with AD dementia, and 39 with other diagnoses. The reference was amyloid PET when available or an approved CSF biomarker profile.
keyResults: Preferred parametric thresholds were ≤0.00370 negative, 0.00371–0.00737 intermediate, and ≥0.00738 positive.
Using the study's nonparametric classification, the ratio yielded 20.2% indeterminate results; p-tau217 alone yielded 35.1%.
For ratio-classified positives, PPV was 94.6% (95% CI, 88.0%–97.7%); the indeterminate group was 47.6% amyloid positive.
whatChanged: A same-sample evaluation supplied implementable dual cutoffs and showed how adding Aβ42 could reduce unresolved classifications on an automated platform.
evidenceStrength: Moderate clinical-validity evidence: clinically relevant cohort and accepted references, but retrospective, single-center, and internally derived thresholds.
clinicalSignificance: The result supports triage logic rather than replacement of CSF or PET. Intermediate results remain common and require a defined follow-up pathway.
fieldRelevance: Useful when discussing why a ratio may change the indeterminate rate, why cutoffs are platform-specific, and why reference modality can influence agreement.

questions.q: Can the ratio replace PET or CSF?
questions.a: Not from this study. It was evaluated against PET or CSF and used a three-zone strategy; intermediate and discordant results still require clinical resolution.

questions.q: Were the thresholds externally validated?
questions.a: No. They were derived in this cohort, so transport to other settings and prevalence levels remains uncertain.

questions.q: Was the ratio clearly superior to p-tau217?
questions.a: It reduced the indeterminate proportion in the same samples. The close AUCs should not be interpreted as universal assay superiority.

limitations: Mixed CSF and PET reference standard
Thresholds derived rather than externally prespecified
Industry relationships and support were reported
platformRelevance: Shows how high-throughput automated immunoassay combinations may improve triage efficiency; it does not compare workflow, cost, or clinical utility against Simoa in a randomized pathway.
accessRelevance: No coverage or patient-cost evidence was evaluated.
citation: Benina N, et al. Clinical validation of the automated Lumipulse G plasma p-tau217/β-amyloid 1-42 ratio. Brain. Published online January 21, 2026. doi:10.1093/brain/awag001.

title: Quanterix announced an FDA 510(k) submission for the five-analyte LucentAD Complete test
bottomLine: Quanterix reported submitting a Simoa-based p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL algorithm to FDA; this was a submission announcement, not a clearance or an independent validation report.
regulatoryStatus: 510(k) submission announced; no FDA clearance verified as of 2026-09-04
brief30: The announcement moved a publicly available five-analyte LDT toward FDA review. The company reported three independent cohorts totaling more than 1,800 symptomatic participants. The release does not provide a decision summary, full contingency tables, or proof of clearance.
studyDesign: Manufacturer-reported regulatory package based on three independent cohorts with more than 1,800 symptomatic participants. Public patient-level methods and complete performance tables were not provided in the announcement.
keyResults: Five reported inputs: p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL.
More than 1,800 symptomatic participants were reported across three independent cohorts.
No FDA decision, authorized intended use, public cutoff table, or independently peer-reviewed pivotal data accompanied the release.
whatChanged: A marketed CLIA LDT was publicly reported as entering FDA premarket review as a multi-analyte algorithmic assay.
evidenceStrength: Regulatory-process evidence only. The submission is verifiable as a company statement; clinical claims remain manufacturer-reported until the FDA record or full study is public.
clinicalSignificance: No clinical practice change follows from a submission alone. FDA review could later clarify intended population, thresholds, limitations, and performance.
fieldRelevance: Use this distinction when asked whether LucentAD Complete is FDA cleared: the test has been offered as an LDT, while the February event was an announced submission.

questions.q: Is LucentAD Complete FDA cleared?
questions.a: No clearance was verified in the FDA database as of September 4, 2026. Quanterix announced a 510(k) submission.

questions.q: Do five analytes prove better clinical performance?
questions.a: No. The release does not provide an appropriate head-to-head comparison showing superiority over a single-marker strategy.

questions.q: Can the test be ordered?
questions.a: The company describes LucentAD Complete as a CLIA laboratory-developed test. Availability is distinct from FDA authorization and from coverage.

limitations: No independent verification of comparative claims
platformRelevance: Directly relevant to Simoa and the transition from an ultrasensitive research platform to centralized clinical testing; it does not establish decentralized implementation.
accessRelevance: A submission does not determine payer coverage, payment, or patient out-of-pocket cost.
citation: Quanterix Corporation. Quanterix announces FDA 510(k) submission for a multi-analyte algorithmic blood test for Alzheimer's disease detection. February 3, 2026.

title: FDA classified a recall of four Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 cartridge lots after falsely elevated results
bottomLine: Affected lots could shift results toward indeterminate or positive classifications and reduce specificity, prompting discontinuation, result review, and clinician notification.
regulatoryStatus: FDA Class II recall; open on the last verified record
brief30: The problem was analytical and operational, not a change in disease biology. Laboratories using affected lots were instructed to stop use and review prior results because positive bias could produce more indeterminate or positive calls.
studyDesign: FDA recall record for a voluntary firm action initiated December 11, 2025 and classified/posting updated in 2026.
keyResults: Four p-tau217 cartridge lots were identified: D4C6028U, D4C6029U, D4C6051U, and D4C6052U.
FDA listed 1,569 affected p-tau217 units distributed in 13 states; the companion ratio recall listed 23 units.
The stated failure mode was falsely elevated p-tau217, with more indeterminate or positive results and lower specificity.
whatChanged: The public record identified a lot-specific source of unexpected positive bias and formalized retrospective result-review actions.
evidenceStrength: High for the existence and scope of the recall; the record does not quantify patient-level false-positive rates.
clinicalSignificance: Unexpected discordance involving affected lots should be evaluated as a potential analytical issue before assuming biological change.
fieldRelevance: Laboratory leaders may ask about lot traceability, corrected reports, clinician notification, and how to separate analytical bias from true blood–CSF–PET discordance.

questions.q: Should an affected result be repeated?
questions.a: The recall record instructs customers to discontinue affected lots and review prior results. The laboratory should follow the manufacturer notice and its corrective-reporting procedure.

questions.q: Does this invalidate all Lumipulse results?
questions.a: No. The action names specific lots; it does not establish a platform-wide failure.

questions.q: How large was the positive bias?
questions.a: The public recall record describes the direction and clinical effect but does not provide a complete patient-level bias distribution.

limitations: Recall database does not provide full root-cause investigation
Status may change and requires re-verification
platformRelevance: Highlights lot control, quality assurance, traceability, and reflex-review requirements for high-throughput biomarker testing.
accessRelevance: Potential repeat testing and corrected reports may create operational burden; no payment guidance was provided.
citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Class 2 Device Recall: LUMIPULSE G pTau 217 Plasma cartridges. Recall Z-1302-2026. Posted February 5, 2026.

title: ADAPT stage 1 externally tested dual p-tau217 cutoffs against amyloid PET
bottomLine: Cutoffs derived against CSF in 257 participants retained roughly 90% definite-result accuracy in a small 76-person PET cohort, but the indeterminate proportion rose to 34% for Lumipulse.
brief30: ADAPT is useful because it separates cutoff derivation from a PET test set and evaluates two platforms. Both strategies preserved high accuracy among definitive results, but the PET validation sample was small and the gray zone expanded, illustrating the implementation cost of high-confidence thresholds.
studyDesign: Stage 1 multicenter study with a 257-person CSF-referenced derivation cohort and an independent 76-person amyloid-PET validation cohort. Dual cutoffs targeted high sensitivity and specificity.
keyResults: CSF-referenced AUC: 0.947 for Lumipulse and 0.940 for ALZpath.
Lumipulse cutoffs 0.153 and 0.422 pg/mL yielded 94.7% accuracy among definite derivation results; PET validation accuracy was 90.0%.
Lumipulse indeterminate results were 19.4% in derivation and 34.2% in PET validation; PET-validation PPV was 90.6% and NPV 88.9%.
ALZpath cutoffs 0.220 and 0.486 pg/mL yielded 93.4% definite-result derivation accuracy and 87.5% PET-validation accuracy; 26.3% were indeterminate in validation.
whatChanged: The study supplied an independent PET test of CSF-derived cutoffs and quantified the tradeoff between confident classification and the size of the intermediate zone.
evidenceStrength: Moderate: multicenter and independent validation, with small PET sample and wide predictive-value intervals.
clinicalSignificance: The results support a triage pathway with an explicit plan for intermediate results, not automatic substitution for PET or CSF.
fieldRelevance: Helpful for explaining why predictive values and gray-zone frequency move when reference method, cohort, and prevalence change.

questions.q: Which assay was better?
questions.a: The study was a same-program comparison, but the small PET set and assay-specific cutoffs do not support a broad superiority claim.

questions.q: What about kidney disease?
questions.a: Reduced eGFR was associated with higher concentrations and movement into the intermediate range, reinforcing the need for contextual interpretation.

questions.q: Are these clinical cutoffs universal?
questions.a: No. They are assay- and population-specific and need prospective pathway validation.

limitations: Different reference standards in derivation and validation
platformRelevance: Direct Simoa–Lumipulse evidence in one development program; analytical sensitivity should not be equated with clinical accuracy.
accessRelevance: A larger indeterminate zone increases downstream PET/CSF use; formal cost-effectiveness was not tested.
citation: Keshavan A, et al. The Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis and Plasma Phospho-Tau217 (ADAPT) study stage 1: validating clinical cut-points against CSF and amyloid PET. Alzheimers Dement. Published online February 19, 2026. doi:10.1002/alz.71147.

title: Longitudinal %p-tau217 models estimated symptom onset within a 3–4 year median error
bottomLine: Research-cohort models linked the estimated age of plasma %p-tau217 positivity to later symptom onset, but they are not validated for individual clinical prognosis or asymptomatic screening.
regulatoryStatus: Research use; no authorized prognostic claim
brief30: Two cohort-specific clock models estimated when %p-tau217 crossed positivity and related that timing to symptom onset. Cross-cohort median absolute error remained about 3–4 years. That is promising for trial design, not a basis for counseling an asymptomatic person to a precise year.
studyDesign: Longitudinal modeling in two selected research cohorts (n=258 and n=345), using serial plasma %p-tau217 and clinical follow-up.
keyResults: Estimated age at %p-tau217 positivity explained 33.7%–61.2% of variance in age at symptom onset across models.
Median absolute error for symptom-onset prediction was 3.0–3.7 years.
Cross-cohort models retained moderate associations, with median absolute error about 3.0–3.7 years.
whatChanged: The work shifted p-tau217 discussion from binary pathology detection toward time-to-symptom modeling.
evidenceStrength: Early prognostic evidence: longitudinal and replicated across two cohorts, but model-based, selected, and not prospectively tested for clinical decisions.
clinicalSignificance: No current screening or individual prognostic use is established. The near-term use case is enrichment and stratification in prevention trials.
fieldRelevance: Expect questions about telling an asymptomatic person when symptoms will begin. The evidence does not support that use.

questions.q: Can one blood draw predict the year symptoms start?
questions.a: No. The median error was measured in years, the cohorts were selected, and the model lacks prospective clinical-utility validation.

questions.q: Is this an approved intended use?
questions.a: No. It is a research prognostic model.

questions.q: Where could it matter first?
questions.a: Trial enrichment and modeling of prevention-study timelines are more plausible near-term applications than routine care.

platformRelevance: Uses mass-spectrometry %p-tau217 and does not establish interchangeability with immunoassay p-tau217 concentrations.
accessRelevance: No coverage or cost-effectiveness evidence; asymptomatic testing can create counseling burdens without an established care pathway.
citation: Schindler SE, et al. Predicting onset of symptomatic Alzheimer's disease with longitudinal plasma %p-tau217. Nat Med. Published online February 19, 2026. doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04206-y.

title: Three p-tau217 platforms were compared head-to-head against amyloid and tau PET
bottomLine: In 113 Japanese participants, all three assays classified amyloid status well, while assay-specific analytical and diagnostic patterns differed; the small, enriched cohort and derived cutoffs limit platform-wide conclusions.
brief30: This is a legitimate same-population comparison: identical samples, both PET modalities, and three platforms. Ella and Lumipulse had higher amyloid-PET AUCs than Simoa in this cohort, while Simoa had the lowest analytical detection range. The result illustrates why analytical sensitivity and diagnostic accuracy are different constructs.
studyDesign: Cross-sectional study of 113 participants (55 AD-continuum, 36 controls, 22 non-AD disorders), all with amyloid and tau PET. Cutoffs were derived in the study using Youden or two-cutoff methods.
keyResults: Ella vs Simoa P=0.009; Lumipulse vs Simoa P=0.019; Ella vs Lumipulse P=0.294.
At derived single cutoffs, sensitivity/specificity were 90.9%/87.9% for Simoa, 92.7%/96.6% for Ella, and 94.6%/94.8% for Lumipulse.
Tau-PET AUCs were 0.937, 0.989, and 0.985, respectively.
whatChanged: A direct comparison quantified platform differences without relying on cross-study AUC comparisons.
evidenceStrength: Moderate for a controlled head-to-head signal; low for general platform selection because the cohort was small and cutoffs were not externally validated.
clinicalSignificance: The data do not establish one universally superior assay. Platform-specific cutoffs, intended use, workflow, and external validation remain decisive.
fieldRelevance: A strong example for explaining why lower LLOQ does not automatically yield better clinical classification and why only same-cohort comparisons support relative claims.

questions.q: Did the study prove one platform is best?
questions.a: No. It found differences in one enriched cohort with derived thresholds. General superiority would require broader, prospectively specified validation.

questions.q: Why did the most analytically sensitive assay not have the highest AUC?
questions.a: Analytical detection limits and diagnostic discrimination answer different questions and are affected by antibody design, calibration, and population.

questions.q: Can the numerical cutoffs be transferred?
questions.a: No. They were platform-specific and derived in this dataset.

limitations: Not a workflow or utility study
platformRelevance: Directly relevant to Simoa, Ella, and Lumipulse; supports precise, bounded comparison rather than broad marketing claims.
accessRelevance: No cost, coverage, turnaround-time, or capacity comparison was performed.
citation: Matsuura S, Tagai K, Tatebe H, et al. Comparison of three plasma p-tau217 assays to detect PET-confirmed Alzheimer's pathologies. Alzheimers Dement (Amst). Published online March 4, 2026. doi:10.1002/dad2.70294.

title: eMTBR-tau243 added symptomatic-disease information after a positive %p-tau217 result
bottomLine: Among symptomatic %p-tau217-positive patients, adding plasma eMTBR-tau243 raised the PPV for established AD from 57% to 84% and identified high tau-PET load with 90% NPV, with similar findings in an external cohort.
regulatoryStatus: Research use; no authorized clinical intended use
brief30: p-tau217 largely marked amyloid pathology, but many positive symptomatic patients did not meet the study's definition of established AD as the cause of symptoms. A second, later-changing tau marker improved stratification. This is a clinically relevant concept, not yet a commercial or guideline-endorsed pathway.
studyDesign: Prospective BioFINDER-2 cohort of 572 symptomatic adults (142 SCD, 259 MCI, 171 dementia), with prespecified biomarker thresholds and external validation in Knight ADRC. Established AD required pathology-specific biomarkers plus a compatible clinical assessment.
keyResults: 350 of 572 were %p-tau217 positive; 341 (97%) were amyloid positive, but 199 (57%) had established AD.
194 of 350 were also eMTBR-tau243 positive; accuracy for established AD was 81% (95% CI, 76%–84%), PPV 84% (78%–88%), NPV 77% (68%–82%), and sensitivity 82% (76%–87%).
Among %p-tau217-positive patients, eMTBR-tau243 identified high tau-PET load with 87% accuracy, 76% PPV, and 90% NPV.
Positive eMTBR-tau243 was associated with faster cognitive decline and tau accumulation.
whatChanged: The study supplied a two-step biological model that separates amyloid confirmation from evidence that more advanced tau pathology may be contributing to symptoms.
evidenceStrength: Moderate-to-strong clinical-validity evidence with prespecified thresholds and external validation; clinical utility remains unproven.
clinicalSignificance: A positive p-tau217 test need not prove that AD is the main cause of symptoms, especially when copathology is plausible. A later-stage tau marker may reduce that ambiguity if validated for clinical use.
fieldRelevance: Directly informs conversations about blood–PET discordance, causality versus copathology, staging, and why one blood marker may not answer every clinical question.

questions.q: Does eMTBR-tau243 replace tau PET?
questions.a: No. It showed association and classification performance against tau-PET-derived states, but clinical substitution and treatment decisions were not tested.

questions.q: Why can p-tau217 be positive when AD is not causing symptoms?
questions.a: p-tau217 is closely linked to amyloid biology and can identify coexisting or earlier AD pathology; symptoms may arise from another disease or a mixed process.

questions.q: Is the two-step pathway available clinically?
questions.a: The reported assays were research mass-spectrometry methods without an authorized clinical intended use.

limitations: Mass-spectrometry assays not routine clinical tests
platformRelevance: Relevant as an emerging marker opportunity, but no Simoa eMTBR-tau243 clinical assay or cross-platform equivalence was established.
accessRelevance: No reimbursement or cost-effectiveness analysis; a two-step pathway could reduce or add downstream testing depending on its final intended use.
citation: Mattsson-Carlgren N, Palmqvist S, Horie K, et al. Integration of plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau217 in the diagnosis and stratification of Alzheimer's disease: a prospective cohort study. Lancet Neurol. 2026;25:357–367. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(26)00029-3.

title: HEAD showed tau PET tracer choice changes how often tau pathology is detected
bottomLine: In 682 paired scans, [18F]MK-6240 detected neocortical tau more often and discriminated AD-related impairment better than flortaucipir, a valid head-to-head result that later informed the Tauklarify landscape.
regulatoryStatus: At publication MK-6240 was investigational; FDA approved it as Tauklarify on 2026-08-13
brief30: This is the kind of comparison that supports a relative performance statement: both tracers were used in the same participants within 45 days. Detection differences could alter staging and trial eligibility. The study did not use autopsy as a universal truth standard and does not make the tracers interchangeable.
studyDesign: Prospective, nonrandomized, cross-sectional study at eight North American sites; 775 enrolled and 682 completed paired tau PET, amyloid PET, and cognitive assessment within 45 days.
keyResults: AUC for AD-related cognitive impairment was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.89–0.95) for MK-6240 versus 0.86 (0.75–0.91) for flortaucipir; P<0.0001.
Neocortical tau positivity in cognitively impaired participants was 28% with MK-6240 versus 16% with flortaucipir.
Among Aβ-positive participants, the prevalence ratio was 1.74 (95% CI, 1.32–2.29).
Regional positivity was concordant in 87% for medial temporal and 94% for neocortical classifications.
whatChanged: The largest paired comparison showed that tracer selection is not a neutral technical detail, particularly for earlier and neocortical tau detection.
evidenceStrength: Strong comparative clinical-validity evidence for the studied imaging definitions; clinical-outcome utility and autopsy accuracy were not primary endpoints.
clinicalSignificance: Tau PET reports and trial criteria should identify the tracer and threshold. Results from one tracer should not be assumed equivalent to another.
fieldRelevance: Expect questions about why the same patient might stage differently by tracer and whether newer tau PET can refine anti-amyloid or anti-tau trial selection.

questions.q: Was this a true head-to-head comparison?
questions.a: Yes. Participants received both tau tracers within 45 days, with the same amyloid and cognitive context.

questions.q: Does more positive mean more accurate?
questions.a: Not automatically. Greater detection and discrimination were shown, but the reference framework was not universal autopsy confirmation.

questions.q: Can studies using the two tracers be pooled directly?
questions.a: Not without tracer-specific harmonization; their binding and dynamic ranges differ.

platformRelevance: Not a blood-assay study, but it affects the imaging reference standard used to validate blood biomarkers and define discordance.
accessRelevance: Tracer distribution, reader training, and PET capacity may determine real-world availability; no payer or cost comparison was tested.
citation: Povala G, Bellaver B, Lussier FZ, et al; HEAD Study. Comparison of [18F]flortaucipir and [18F]MK6240 for the detection of tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease. Lancet. Published online May 28, 2026. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00417-4.

title: Anthem revised LAB.00046 to make qualifying blood biomarker testing medically necessary
bottomLine: The July policy established criteria-based medical necessity for symptomatic adults aged 50 or older using an FDA-cleared test or p-tau217/%p-tau217, while excluding asymptomatic screening and repeat testing without a new indication.
brief30: The policy is broader than FDA-cleared tests because it also permits tests measuring p-tau217 or %p-tau217 when all clinical criteria are met. It is not a blanket payment guarantee: benefit language, coding, medical-necessity review, and member contract still control.
studyDesign: Medical policy reviewed May 14 and published July 1, 2026. It covers biochemical CSF and blood biomarkers and explicitly excludes PET from this policy.
keyResults: Required: measurable MCI or dementia with insidious progressive decline, unclear diagnosis after standard evaluation, and an expected management impact.
For blood tests: age ≥50, FDA clearance/approval or measurement of p-tau217/%p-tau217, plus a triage, CSF-infeasible, or referral use.
Asymptomatic screening and repeat testing without a new indication are not medically necessary.
The coding section lists 0479U (ALZpath pTau217), 0503U (PrecivityAD2), and 0568U (LucentAD Complete), but coding does not itself guarantee payment.
whatChanged: A major payer moved specified blood biomarker testing from noncoverage to criteria-based medical necessity.
evidenceStrength: High for the policy terms; plan-level applicability, adjudication, and paid claims require separate verification.
clinicalSignificance: Coverage criteria favor symptomatic, decision-relevant triage and do not endorse population screening or serial monitoring.
fieldRelevance: Useful for questions about documentation, age, use case, coding, and why medical necessity is distinct from FDA status and payment amount.

questions.q: Does this mean every Anthem member is covered?
questions.a: No. The policy states that federal/state law and each member's contract take precedence; prior authorization and plan adoption may vary.

questions.q: Are LDTs eligible?
questions.a: The criterion allows either an FDA-cleared/approved test or one measuring p-tau217/%p-tau217, provided all other conditions are met.

questions.q: Does a listed CPT or PLA code guarantee reimbursement?
questions.a: No. The policy expressly says code inclusion does not imply coverage or payment.

limitations: Policy applicability varies by plan and jurisdiction
The FDA-status note became outdated after August 2026 clearances
platformRelevance: The criteria encompass p-tau217 approaches across platforms and list LucentAD Complete's PLA code; that is not a comparative endorsement.
accessRelevance: Potentially reduces access barriers for qualifying symptomatic members, but negotiated payment and patient cost are not stated.
citation: Anthem. LAB.00046: Testing for Biochemical Markers for Alzheimer Disease. Published July 1, 2026; last reviewed May 14, 2026.

title: A 49,227-person meta-analysis defined an 11–26 Centiloid caution zone for amyloid PET
bottomLine: Across 53 studies, values below 11 Centiloids were high-confidence negative and values above 26 high-confidence positive in a data-driven model; the 11–26 range warrants contextual interpretation rather than an automatic binary call.
regulatoryStatus: Quantitative evidence; visual reading and tracer labels remain controlling
brief30: This large analysis gives a defensible framework for talking about borderline amyloid PET quantitation. It does not replace expert visual interpretation and showed substantial between-study heterogeneity. A blood, CSF, or repeat imaging result may be useful when quantitation and visual read disagree.
studyDesign: Individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 49,227 scans from 53 studies and five tracers in 15 countries. Gaussian mixture and visual-read correspondence methods were analyzed separately.
keyResults: Data-driven single positivity cutoff: 18 Centiloids (95% CI, 16–19; I²=97%).
Double cutoff: <11 high-confidence negative (95% CI, 9–13) and >26 high-confidence positive (24–28); I²=95% for both.
Visual-read correspondence in 35,045 scans produced a 27-Centiloid cutoff (95% CI, 24–30) and κ=0.86 (0.83–0.89).
The intermediate range was 11–26 Centiloids.
whatChanged: The field gained pooled quantitative benchmarks and an explicit indeterminate interval rather than another single-study threshold.
evidenceStrength: Strong quantitative synthesis with high heterogeneity and no single harmonized visual-read protocol.
clinicalSignificance: Borderline Centiloid values should be treated as uncertainty, especially when used for diagnosis or treatment eligibility.
fieldRelevance: Relevant to interpreting blood–PET discordance and to explaining why a binary threshold may not reflect the uncertainty near the decision boundary.

questions.q: Can 18 Centiloids be used as the universal positive cutoff?
questions.a: No. It is a meta-estimate with high heterogeneity; method, tracer, visual read, and intended use matter.

questions.q: Should quantitation override the visual read?
questions.a: No. The authors state that expert visual assessment remains crucial.

questions.q: What should happen in the 11–26 range?
questions.a: Review scan quality and visual interpretation and consider another validated biomarker when uncertainty would change management.

limitations: Limited representation from several world regions
Not a randomized clinical utility study
platformRelevance: Defines uncertainty in a common reference used for blood-assay validation; discordance may reflect PET threshold choice rather than blood-assay error alone.
accessRelevance: Clarifying intermediate scans may require additional testing; no cost analysis was performed.
citation: Blazhenets G, Soleimani-Meigooni DN, Chiotis K, et al. Amyloid PET quantitation and Centiloid thresholds in the diagnosis of Alzheimer disease. JAMA. Published online July 13, 2026. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.13116.

title: Pooled cohorts linked very high p-tau217 to 38% five-year progression risk in unimpaired adults
bottomLine: Among 2,684 selected cognitively unimpaired participants, very high p-tau217 was associated with 38% five-year absolute risk of cognitive impairment, but the authors cautioned against individual prognosis in unselected populations.
assays: Multiple plasma p-tau217 assays, harmonized within cohort
regulatoryStatus: Research use; no asymptomatic screening or prognostic claim authorized
brief30: The study provides absolute rather than only relative risk, which is useful for prevention-trial planning. It does not justify routine testing of asymptomatic people: cohorts were selected, assay values were standardized within study, and longer-horizon estimates were sparse.
studyDesign: Harmonized analysis of 2,684 cognitively unimpaired participants across six North American, Japanese, and Australian cohorts; median follow-up 5.4 years and maximum 13.5 years.
keyResults: 478 participants progressed to cognitive impairment.
Per 1-SD higher baseline p-tau217, HR 1.38 (95% CI, 1.30–1.46); adjusted for amyloid PET Centiloids, HR 1.32 (1.24–1.41).
Five-year absolute risk was 24% (95% CI, 20%–28%) for high and 38% (33%–43%) for very high p-tau217.
Very-high group annualized PACC change was −0.07 units/year versus +0.03 in the low group.
whatChanged: The report translated p-tau217 into time-specific absolute progression risk across multiple cohorts.
evidenceStrength: Moderate prognostic evidence with multicohort consistency; clinical utility and calibration in unselected care populations remain unknown.
clinicalSignificance: Most people in the very-high group did not progress within five years. A high result is not a diagnosis or a deterministic forecast.
fieldRelevance: Expect questions from clinicians and researchers about screening, counseling, and prevention-trial enrollment. Keep research prognosis separate from approved diagnostic intended use.

questions.q: Should asymptomatic adults get p-tau217 testing?
questions.a: Not on this evidence. The study calls for validation in unselected populations and does not establish a care pathway or benefit from disclosure.

questions.q: Does 38% mean a person has a 38% personal risk?
questions.a: It is a group estimate in selected cohorts, not a fully calibrated individual prediction.

questions.q: Does p-tau217 add beyond amyloid PET?
questions.a: The association persisted after Centiloid adjustment, but incremental decision value and utility were not tested.

platformRelevance: Cross-assay harmonization by SD does not make concentrations or cutoffs interchangeable across platforms.
accessRelevance: No evidence supports payer coverage for asymptomatic prognostic testing; downstream counseling and confirmatory testing could be substantial.
citation: Buckley RF, Townsend DL, Birkenbihl CJ, et al. Prognostic value of blood-based p-tau217 levels for progression to cognitive impairment. JAMA. Published online July 14, 2026. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.12556.

title: A prospective memory-clinic study found modest diagnostic changes but higher confidence after BBM disclosure
bottomLine: In 450 specialty-clinic patients, a p-tau181/GFAP/NfL panel changed the suspected etiology in 5% and raised median diagnostic confidence from 80% to 90%; intermediate results were common.
regulatoryStatus: Research implementation; panel was not an FDA-authorized diagnostic
brief30: This study measured actual diagnostic workflow impact, not just AUC. The panel most often changed confidence rather than the diagnosis. Because it used p-tau181 and academic specialty clinics, it should not be assumed to predict the impact of current p-tau217 workflows or primary care.
studyDesign: Consecutive prospective cohort at three Dutch academic memory clinics; blood results were presented after standard workup during multidisciplinary meetings, with later CSF/PET disclosure when available.
keyResults: N=450; 149 SCD, 67 MCI, 162 dementia, and other syndromes.
Median diagnostic confidence rose from 80% (IQR 70%–90%) to 90% (70%–90%); P<0.001.
Etiologic diagnosis changed in 23 patients (5%); syndrome diagnosis changed in 6 (1%).
Among 356 evaluated for AD probability, 42% were high, 28% intermediate, and 30% low. In the CSF/PET subset, intermediate results occurred in 24%–39% depending on the model.
whatChanged: The field gained prospective evidence about how a multimarker panel altered real multidisciplinary decisions and confidence.
evidenceStrength: Moderate implementation evidence; no randomized comparator, incomplete reference testing, and an older p-tau marker constrain causal conclusions.
clinicalSignificance: Biomarkers may refine confidence even when they rarely change diagnosis. A high intermediate rate can blunt practical value and create downstream testing.
fieldRelevance: Directly relevant to questions from memory clinics and health systems about where in the workflow to reveal results and what outcome to measure.

questions.q: Did the panel improve diagnostic accuracy?
questions.a: The main result was change in diagnosis and confidence, not a randomized improvement in patient outcomes. Reference testing was available in only 52%.

questions.q: Will p-tau217 have the same impact?
questions.a: Unknown. The authors note that p-tau217 may reduce intermediate results, but that workflow requires prospective testing.

questions.q: Is this primary-care evidence?
questions.a: No. It was conducted in academic specialty memory clinics.

limitations: Only 52% had CSF or amyloid PET
Quanterix employee coauthor and disclosed relationships
platformRelevance: Direct example of Simoa multianalyte use in a diagnostic workflow; does not establish an authorized panel or a commercial superiority claim.
accessRelevance: No reimbursement or economic endpoint; intermediate classifications may add confirmatory testing.
citation: Vigneswaran S, Verberk IMW, Boonkamp L, et al. Plasma Alzheimer biomarkers and diagnostic decision-making in memory clinics. JAMA Netw Open. 2026;9:e2628864. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.28864.

title: FDA approved Tauklarify as a second tau PET tracer for cognitively impaired adults
bottomLine: Florquinitau F 18 (formerly MK-6240) is now approved to identify tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology in adults with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD, with label cautions against standalone exclusion or confirmation.
evidenceSource: FDA approval and official sponsor release
brief30: The United States now has a second approved tau PET tracer. Its pivotal reader studies used a prespecified reference based on cognitive status and amyloid PET—not universal autopsy. A negative scan does not exclude tau pathology, especially earlier disease, and use in non-AD tauopathies is not established.
studyDesign: Two blinded image-reader studies with five readers per study and 617 total participants: 152 mild AD dementia, 157 MCI, and 308 cognitively unimpaired.
keyResults: Study 1 (n=279): reader positive percent agreement 80%–88% and negative percent agreement 98%–99%.
Study 2 (n=338): positive percent agreement 68%–82% and negative percent agreement 93%–99%.
Generalized Fleiss κ was 0.92 and 0.86 in the two studies.
Safety exposure included 1,734 participants; headache was reported in 0.7%.
whatChanged: MK-6240 moved from research use to an FDA-approved radiodiagnostic intended for cognitively impaired adults under AD evaluation.
evidenceStrength: High for authorization and reader reproducibility; reference-standard and early-stage sensitivity limitations remain material.
clinicalSignificance: Tau PET choice may now expand beyond flortaucipir, but ordering, reading, distribution, and payer pathways need implementation.
fieldRelevance: Expect questions about differences from Tauvid, early tau detection, staging, and whether tau PET is required for anti-amyloid therapy. Keep label claims separate from research comparisons.

questions.q: Can a negative Tauklarify scan rule out AD tau?
questions.a: No. The label cautions that performance may be lower earlier in the pathological spectrum and a negative scan does not necessarily exclude tau pathology.

questions.q: Is it approved for PSP, CTE, or other tauopathies?
questions.a: No. Safety and effectiveness for non-AD tauopathies have not been established.

questions.q: Is it proven superior to Tauvid?
questions.a: The separate HEAD study found direct comparative differences, but the FDA approval itself does not create a universal superiority claim across all uses.

limitations: Reference combined cognition and amyloid PET rather than universal autopsy
Real-world availability and coverage not established in the approval
platformRelevance: Changes the PET reference landscape used for blood- and CSF-biomarker studies.
accessRelevance: Approval does not establish local tracer supply, PET capacity, payer coverage, or patient cost.
citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Tauklarify (florquinitau F 18) novel drug approval. Approved August 13, 2026.

title: FDA cleared the PrecivityAD2 mass-spectrometry blood test
bottomLine: The cleared test combines Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau217/np-tau217 into an Amyloid Probability Score 2 for symptomatic adults aged 40 or older; current LDT availability and rollout of the cleared IVD remain distinct.
evidenceSource: FDA 510(k) decision and official company announcement
brief30: FDA clearance adds a mass-spectrometry approach with dual cutoffs to the authorized blood-test landscape. The intended population begins at age 40 and requires symptoms plus experienced clinical assessment. C2N states that the cleared product rollout is forthcoming; the currently offered PrecivityAD2 LDT is not automatically the same regulatory product.
studyDesign: Pivotal clinical validation reported by C2N in 1,142 symptomatic participants, using amyloid PET as reference and a dual-cutoff APS2 interpretation.
keyResults: FDA 510(k) K253240 decision date: August 19, 2026.
Reported clinical validation n=1,142.
Reported positive-category PPV 97.6% and negative-category NPV 93.1%.
The 'Likely Positive' intermediate category was 17.3% of participants and had PPV 77.3%.
whatChanged: A laboratory mass-spectrometry algorithm became an FDA-cleared IVD aid for amyloid-pathology assessment.
evidenceStrength: High for regulatory status; detailed subgroup and analytical interpretation should follow the FDA decision summary and final labeling.
clinicalSignificance: The result is an aid, not standalone diagnosis. The intermediate group remains clinically meaningful and prevalence affects predictive value.
fieldRelevance: Expect questions about LDT versus cleared IVD, sample shipping, turnaround, age range, algorithm transparency, and comparison with automated immunoassays.

questions.q: Is the FDA-cleared version available today?
questions.a: C2N states that availability of the cleared test is expected in coming months; the currently available test is described as an LDT. Verify at ordering.

questions.q: Can it replace PET or CSF?
questions.a: The clearance is as an aid in assessment, not a standalone diagnosis. Intermediate or discordant results may still require confirmatory evaluation.

questions.q: Can APS2 be compared directly with an immunoassay concentration?
questions.a: No. It combines multiple mass-spectrometry ratios in a proprietary score with its own thresholds and intended use.

limitations: Predictive values depend on study prevalence
Algorithm-specific score is not cross-platform interchangeable
platformRelevance: Adds a centralized mass-spectrometry model to the clinical landscape; comparisons with immunoassays require same-cohort evidence.
accessRelevance: Clearance does not establish payer coverage, payment, shipping logistics, or patient cost.
citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. PrecivityAD2 Test. 510(k) K253240. Decision August 19, 2026.

title: FDA cleared Elecsys pTau217 Plasma with fixed negative, intermediate, and positive cutoffs
bottomLine: In 958 valid participants aged 55 or older, the automated assay produced PPV 88.5%, NPV 95.3%, and 19.9% intermediate results against amyloid PET, with lower positive predictive value in primary care.
brief30: The decision summary supplies public cutoffs, subgroup performance, and analytical data for a fully automated single-analyte test. Lower prevalence in primary care reduced PPV, illustrating why the same cutoff does not produce the same post-test probability in every setting.
studyDesign: Retrospective pivotal analysis of 958 valid symptomatic participants aged 55–85 years; 378 amyloid-PET positive and 580 negative. About 25% were from primary care and 75% from specialty settings.
keyResults: Cutoffs: ≤0.223 pg/mL negative; >0.223 to ≤0.378 intermediate; >0.378 positive.
Positive category: 285/322 amyloid positive, PPV 88.5% (95% CI, 84.9%–91.4%). Negative category: 424/445 amyloid negative, NPV 95.3% (93.1%–96.8%).
191/958 (19.9%) were intermediate; 72/191 (37.7%) were amyloid positive.
Primary-care PPV was 78.3% versus 90.2% in secondary/tertiary care. Measuring range was 0.056–2.40 pg/mL; within-lab CV was about 1.2%–5.0%.
whatChanged: A high-throughput, single-analyte p-tau217 assay gained a public FDA intended use and fixed three-zone interpretation across primary and specialty settings.
evidenceStrength: High regulatory and clinical-validity evidence with public analytical and subgroup data; prospective clinical utility is not established.
clinicalSignificance: The test may aid amyloid-pathology assessment but cannot be used alone. Intermediate results and positive results near the cutoff may require PET or CSF depending on context.
fieldRelevance: The decision summary provides concrete answers on prevalence, predictive value, cutoffs, sample handling, and primary-care generalizability.

questions.q: Can this replace PET or CSF?
questions.a: Not universally. The label says it is an aid and not standalone; intermediate and some positive results require clinical follow-up.

questions.q: Why is PPV lower in primary care?
questions.a: Amyloid prevalence was lower. Predictive value changes with pretest probability even when assay sensitivity and specificity are unchanged.

questions.q: Can it be used to monitor treatment?
questions.a: No monitoring or prediction claim is established in the cleared intended use.

limitations: Subgroup confidence intervals widen for underrepresented groups
Clinical utility and serial monitoring not tested
platformRelevance: Important automated-laboratory comparator for ultrasensitive platforms; performance claims must remain within the same intended use and reference.
accessRelevance: Roche and Quest announced future rollout, but clearance alone does not establish current local availability, coverage, or payment.
citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Elecsys Phospho-Tau (217P) Plasma. 510(k) K261686. Decision August 19, 2026.
